# Review — iliad-078 (Iliad 13.81–168)

Reviewer, two passes. `t` untouched in every unit (checked: the units' `t` joined equals the edition's lines 81–168 word for word; every `ln` and every `p` matches the edition's line and paragraph starts; speech marks balanced, “ on 95 and 150, ” on 123 and 154, `mark` on both opening units, and the previous part ends with Ajax's speech already closed at 79).

Severity: high = wrong sense, wrong claim a reader would carry away, or a breach of a fixed house rendering; medium = false grammatical label, a table conformity slip, or a misleading note; low = cosmetic or a loose statement.

## Pass 1 — units.json

Totals: 2 high, 6 medium, 3 low (11 changes). Plus three rows of `new-renderings.md` brought into line with them.

| line (unit) | field | severity | what was wrong | what was done |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 139 (ἀναιδέος πέτρης) | `i` | high | “pitiless” for a rock. The table already fixes the rock: λᾶας ἀναιδής (4.521, from Odyssey 11.598) is `l` “shameless”, `i` “ruthless”, and the Odyssey table turns “pitiless” down for ἀναιδής. The drafter listed “ruthless” as avoided and filed a new rendering for something already settled. | `i` “ruthless”. |
| 139 | `n` | medium | Note defended “pitiless”. | Now “‘ruthless’ in the English, the table’s word for a stone (4.521)”. `new-renderings.md` row rewritten as “follows the table unchanged”. |
| 166 (ὃ ξυνέαξε) | `n` | high | Note said ὅ might be the *subject* (“the spear broke”). ξυνέαξε is the transitive aorist (ἔαξα); the intransitive “break” is ἐάγη, which the poet used four lines earlier. So ὅ can only be the object, and the subject is what stays open. | Note rewritten: ὅ is the object, the aorist is transitive, who or what shattered it is not said. |
| 166 | `l` | medium | “which broke up” reads as the spear breaking by itself, the very reading the Greek does not allow. | `l` “which was broken up” (open subject, as `i` “had been shattered”). `new-renderings.md` row updated. |
| 105–106 (οὐδ’ ἠβαιόν) | `i` | medium | “not even a little”. Table row οὐδ’ ἠβαιόν (2.380, 2.386): `l` “not even a little”, `i` “not the least bit”; the row lists “not even a little” in `i` as turned down. | `i` “not the least bit”. |
| 129–130 (φράξαντες δόρυ δουρί, σάκος σάκεϊ) | `n` | medium | Note called δόρυ and σάκος “datives”. They are the accusative objects; δουρί and σάκεϊ are the datives. | Note now names the accusatives and the datives correctly. |
| 89 (ἔφαν) | `n` | medium | “ἔφαν is the aorist of φημί”, stated flatly. The form is the past of φημί that the glossary (and Smyth) take as imperfect; calling it aorist alone is a false label. | “imperfect”. |
| 156 (Δηΐφοβος) | `n` | medium | “Deiphobus comes into the story”: he has already been named among the Trojan leaders at 12.94 (Ἕλενος καὶ Δηΐφοβος). | “named once before among the Trojan leaders (12.94), now has a part of his own; he is a son of Priam, and not Hector.” |
| 127–128 (λαοσσόος) | `n` | low | “is the Odyssey’s word for Athena”. The Odyssey table has λαοσσόος only of Amphiaraus (15.244); the Odyssey never says it of Athena. | “follows the Odyssey table’s λαοσσόος, there said of Amphiaraus”. |
| 131 (ἀσπὶς ἄρ’ ἀσπίδ’) | `l` | low | “Shield” capitalised, but the unit before ends at a semicolon and the Greek has a stop only in the middle of the line. | lower case “shield”. |
| 95 (αἰδὼς Ἀργεῖοι) | `i` | low | “Shame on you, Argives” departs from the table’s `i` of the same words (5.787: “Shame, Argives, …”) without need. | `i` “Shame, Argives, you young men!”. `new-renderings.md` row updated. |

### Cross-references checked (all against the edition text and the table)

12.469 (ὑπέρβασαν τεῖχος: the same crossing, true); 12.121 (μακρὸν ὀχῆα, true); 5.787 (αἰδὼς Ἀργεῖοι, true); 5.274 (identical line, and it is the same line as iliad-029, so the English is the published English: checked, equal); 2.235 (ὦ πέπονες, row says “O good ones” / “My good fellows”: matches). Also checked and true: 4.234 (θούριδος ἀλκῆς), 1.228 (κὴρ εἴδεται), 2.470, 2.387, 2.368, 2.214, 2.365, 1.162, 5.498, 11.296, 12.339, 12.453, 3.362, 9.541, 1.11, 12.94 (new), Odyssey “beneath the brows” (odyssey-015, -033, -038, -079) and “grievous as you are” (odyssey-088). Line 13.81 = 5.274, 13.107, 13.112, 13.149, 13.150, 13.155 and 13.167: no whole unit coincides with a published one except 149 and 155, whose `l`/`i` are identical to the published ones; 167 reuses the published wording for its line.

### Findings considered and refused

- **Line 164 scansion flag (`UNRESOLVED`, “metrical lengthening: Μηριόναο [longum of foot 3]”).** Scanned by hand: ἔγ-χος | Μη-ρι-ό | να-ο ‖ δα | ΐ-φρο-νος | αὐ-τὰρ-ὅ | γ’ἥ-ρως, i.e. spondee, four dactyls, final spondee, 16 syllables, with the feminine caesura of the third foot. It is regular. The “lengthening” is the genitive in -αο, whose α is long (the same α stands long at the end of the line in Ἀτρεΐδαο, 1.203, 9.388, and the scanner scans those without a licence); the flag appears only because the scanner does not know the quantity of the α in Μηριόναο (the same flag stands on 17.610 and 23.877). The ΐ of δαΐφρονος is long before φρ, as in every line with that word. No irregularity, so no sentence added to the note.
- ὄτρυνε called “aorist” in the notes at 90, 143 and 155, while the glossary calls it imperfect: the form is ambiguous (unaugmented), the house has written both, and `l`/`i` (“urged on”) fit either. Left.
- 153 `i` “before my spear” where the Greek has only ὑπ’ ἔγχεος: the possessive is the obvious sense (Hector’s own spear) and `l` keeps the bare “the spear”. Left.
- Note at 90 says ῥεῖα is the epic ῥέα, and at 144 ῥέα is the epic ῥεῖα: each names the form the line prints against the other; both are true. Left.
- 117–119 `i` “a sorry creature as he is” against the Odyssey `i` “grievous as you are” (odyssey-088): a departure, but already recorded in `new-renderings.md` with its reason, and the Greek context (a man who slackens in war) does forbid the Odyssey’s phrase.
- “The ‘fight’ is a quarrel or a rebuke, not a battle” (note at 117): an interpretation, hedged in the note's own wording and the usual reading. Left.
- ἀπητίμησε in the glossary as “ἀπατιμάω”: the lemma is a reconstruction (ἀπ- + ἀτιμάω); meaning and parse are right and the entry is not misleading. Left.
- σχήσουσιν glossed “(= Attic ἕξω)”: Attic also has σχήσω; the entry equates the meaning, not the spelling, and does not call it epic. Left.
- νέοι (voc., 95): the known entry gives the nominative; the form is identical and the use (adjective in address) is covered by “adj., agreeing with …”. Left.
- χειρῶν (134): looked like a gap but the known entry already has “of separation after ἀπό: θρασειάων ἀπὸ χειρῶν”. Not broadened.
- Pass-1 reading of Greek → `l` → `i` word by word: no further errors in case, tense, mood or particles; remembered-English check: no phrase that looked ready-made except the stock lines, which follow the table.

## Pass 2 — gloss.json

gloss.json held 106 novel forms (the same keys as `novel-forms.json`, none missing, none extra, longest entry 139 characters) and 13 `__broaden__` entries. Every parse was checked against the line it occurs in; the known forms were also checked for uses the old entries do not cover.

Totals: 0 high, 2 medium, 5 low (7 changes).

| form | severity | what was wrong | what was done |
|---|---|---|---|
| παρδαλίων | medium | “masc. gen. pl.”: πάρδαλις is feminine. | “fem. gen. pl.”. |
| θαῦμα (broaden) | medium | The known entry has only “neut. nom. sg., in apposition”; at 99 it is the accusative object of ὁρῶμαι. | `__broaden__` entry added: old entry whole + “ · also neut. acc. sg., object of ὁρῶμαι: ’a wonder’”. |
| δεινόν (broaden) | low | New reading said “adj. in apposition to a clause”; at 99 δεινόν agrees with θαῦμα (as the unit's own note says). | “adj. agreeing with θαῦμα: ’a dreadful (wonder)’”. |
| πέλονται (broaden) | low | Old entry gives only “they go, extend”; at 103 the verb is the copula (“are, become” food). | Reading added to `__broaden__`. |
| εἷος (broaden) | low | Old parse gives only “while”; at 141 it is “until” with the aorist subjunctive. | Reading added to `__broaden__`. |
| διελεύσεσθαι | low | “epic fut. stem ἐλευσ- (= Attic διελεύσεσθαι)”: equates the form with itself and wrongly marks the stem epic. | “fut. inf. mid. (fut. stem ἐλευσ-), + acc.”. |
| λαοσσόος | low | Derivation stated as settled, though the note and the Odyssey entry say it is disputed. | “(λαός + σεύω; derivation disputed)”. |

Parses checked and left (no error): the other 103 novel entries (case, number, gender, tense, voice and mood each match the line), and the other 12 broadened entries (αὐτοῖο, μάχεσθαι, μεθίετε, Πριαμίδης, στεφάνης, τιτύσκετο, τῇδε, χάρμῃ, ἁμάς, ἡγεμόνος, ὑπ’, ὑπὸ: each new reading is true of the line cited). The glossary is general to the form, has no line numbers and uses only ’.
